title: #leftontenth #leftontenthbway #leftontenthbroadway #leftontenthplay #...
transcript: Last night, I saw Left On Tenth, a new play on Broadway that's a bit of a catfish — a would-be tear-jerker disguised as a rom-com. Based on a memoir by Delia Ephron and told mostly through her point of view, this is a story of love and persistence and fearlessness in the face of uncertainty time and time again. I wanna preface my critiques by acknowledging that I'm definitely not the target demographic here, and I think book to stage adaptations are generally difficult to execute well, but I unfortunately felt that this story's transition from page to stage was pretty clunky. Delia’s personal stakes don't translate into dramatic stakes, and even at just 100 minutes the play feels pretty drawn out. The tone was also kind of weird to me, like things were fun and lighthearted initially, but then not serious when I think they were supposed to be. Leading actors Julianna Margulies and Peter Gallagher have great chemistry and the play does have a small handful of genuinely touching moments but nothing about it was particularly distinctive to me. Some stories, I would argue this being one of them, are best kept as chapters rather than scenes delivered in one sitting. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer finds the adaptation 'clunky,' feels it drags at 100 minutes, notes tonal issues, and concludes the story is better as a book than a play. While acknowledging some chemistry and touching moments, the overall assessment is clearly negative with no recommendation.
